text: A U.S. Navy lab came up with the idea behind the dark web's best-known network.
Nineteen ninety-five. Three researchers at the Naval Research Laboratory called it onion routing.
Your connection gets wrapped in layers and passed through at least three other computers, so nobody watching can tell who's talking to whom.
In 2002 it went live as a free network, named Tor: The Onion Routing.
So why would a navy build a way to hide on the internet? And who actually uses it?
Both answers are in level three of the full video. Tap the link.
